__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus instance scraping the perf-sentinel daemon /metrics endpoint.

links.title: perf-sentinel dashboards
links.tooltip: The companion dashboard sharing the perf-sentinel tag: perf-sentinel findings reads the query API and answers which operation on which endpoint.

panels.title: I/O ops rate by service
panels.description: Database queries and outbound HTTP calls made by each instrumented service, per second. This is the raw workload perf-sentinel measures, before any judgement about whether the calls were needed. Use it to see which service dominates I/O: a service that is loud here and also appears in the findings panels is where optimisation pays most.

panels.title: Slow span duration p95 by kind
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of spans that crossed the slow threshold (500 ms by default, configurable). Only slow spans enter this histogram, so the value is always above that threshold by construction and is not your overall latency. Split by kind: sql, http_out and messaging. Aggregated with histogram_quantile so it stays correct across sharded daemons.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(perf_sentinel_slow_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping", type="sql"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(perf_sentinel_slow_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping", type="http_out"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(perf_sentinel_slow_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping", type="messaging"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Top 10 finding types by severity
panels.description: A finding is one detected inefficiency, for example an N+1 loop (the same query repeated once per row instead of a single batched one). This ranks the most frequent kinds This ranks the most frequent kinds over the selected time range. Rising counts mean either new traffic reaching an unoptimised path, or a recent deploy that regressed.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (type, severity) (increase(perf_sentinel_findings_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Slow span duration distribution
panels.description: Heatmap of slow span buckets over time, complementing the global p95 panel with the full duration distribution. Hot bands above the p95 line indicate tail latency drift.

panels.title: I/O waste ratio
panels.description: Share of I/O operations attributed to avoidable anti-patterns, over the selected time range and summed across every replica. Both counters are analysis-side, from the same scoring pass and under the same 128-service cap (overflow folds into service="_other", both silent when green scoring is off) and the same 512-pair cap on (service, grouping) pairs (grouping="_other"), so the ratio never mixes populations. Derived from the two counters rather than read off the `perf_sentinel_io_waste_ratio` gauge: that gauge is a ratio of lifetime counters, so it ignores the time picker, dilutes a current problem in everything since the pod started, and renders one dial per replica. Two decimals because a fleet doing 1% avoidable I/O on a million operations is worth seeing, and integer percent would round it to zero.

targets.expr: sum(increase(perf_sentinel_service_avoidable_io_ops_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping"}[$__range])) / (sum(increase(perf_sentinel_service_analyzed_io_ops_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping"}[$__range])) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Critical findings
panels.description: Findings the analyzer rated critical, over the selected time range. Severity comes from how far the pattern exceeds its detection threshold, not from user impact, so a critical finding is a strong optimisation candidate rather than an outage. Shows 0 rather than 'no data' when none were emitted, so a flat zero line means healthy and not broken: unless the selected service was folded past the 128-service analysis cap, in which case its findings count under service="_other", and likewise a (service, grouping) pair past the 512-pair cap counts under grouping="_other".

targets.expr: sum(increase(perf_sentinel_findings_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping", severity="critical"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Findings distribution by type
panels.description: The same findings as the ranking panel, shown as a share of the whole. Answers 'what kind of problem does this system mostly have'. A single type dominating usually points at one framework or one query pattern rather than at a broad problem. A type missing from the legend had no increase over the range, which is not the same as never emitted: after a deploy, the replaced instance's series would otherwise linger in the legend at zero.

panels.title: Total findings (cumulative)
panels.description: Findings emitted since daemon start for the selected services (the grand total with All selected), summed across all types and severities. Pairs with the per-type / per-severity panels to give a single at-a-glance number.

panels.title: Ingested I/O ops (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative count of ingested I/O operations since the daemon started, per service (counted at ingest admission, before the analysis queue: an analysis stall does not flatten it, watch perf_sentinel_analysis_queue_depth and the shed counters for that). Ops past the 1024-service ingest cap are dropped, not folded; (service, grouping) pairs past the 4096-pair cap fold their grouping into grouping="_other". If it stops climbing while traffic continues, ingestion has stalled. It resets on restart.

panels.title: Avoidable I/O ops rate
panels.description: Operations per second that the analyzer marked as avoidable, meaning the same result could have been obtained with fewer calls. This is the GreenOps trend signal: unlike the cumulative waste ratio it reacts immediately, so it is the panel that shows an optimisation PR landing.

panels.title: Findings rate by type
panels.description: Findings emitted per second, by type, for the selected grouping and services: the same counter the ranking, the pie and the table read over the whole range, here as a trend, so a deploy that regressed or fixed a path shows as a step at the moment it landed. The only panel with exemplars enabled. With exemplar storage on Prometheus and a trace datasource mapped in Grafana (docs/HELM-DEPLOYMENT.md, Exemplars), each series carries diamonds linking to the worst trace of its (type, severity, service, grouping), kept for 15 minutes after the batch that recorded it. Without that setup the diamonds are absent and the counts are the same.

panels.title: Findings detail by type and severity
panels.description: Tabular breakdown of finding counts grouped by (type, severity) over the selected time range, the same window as the ranking and distribution panels beside it, so the three never contradict each other. Useful for raw triage, copy-paste into tickets, and comparing relative magnitude across detection categories side by side. The cumulative grand total since daemon start is the 'Total findings (cumulative)' stat.

targets.expr: sum by (type, severity) (increase(perf_sentinel_findings_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"$service", grouping=~"$grouping"}[$__range])) > 0

panels.title: Service silence (time since last span)
panels.description: Seconds since the daemon last received a span for each service. A traffic signal, not a liveness one: a crash, a scale to zero, a rolling deploy and a quiet cron all look the same, so alert on it with a `for:` longer than the service's normal idle gap. Rising here beside a flat findings rate is the shape of a service that stopped, and the window to hand to /api/findings?since_ms=&until_ms=.

panels.title: Daemon health
panels.description: up{} for the perf-sentinel daemon scrape job. 0 means Prometheus cannot reach /metrics. Adjust the job label to match your ServiceMonitor / scrape_configs naming.

panels.title: Traces analyzed (cumulative)
panels.description: Traces that completed analysis since daemon start. Trace-level cadence, where 'events processed' is span-level. The ratio between the two gives the average trace size, which is a useful sanity check on your instrumentation coverage.

panels.title: Active traces
panels.description: Distributed traces currently held in memory waiting to be completed. A trace is released for analysis once it expires (30s by default) or the window is full. A stable plateau is healthy. Continuous growth means traces arrive faster than they expire, and the cap will start dropping the oldest ones, see the headroom panel.

panels.title: Ingest memory pressure
panels.description: perf_sentinel_ingest_memory_pressure, 1 while the cgroup admission guard refuses ingest (HTTP 503, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, both retryable) to keep RSS under the memory limit, the gauge PerfSentinelMemoryPressureRejecting fires on after 5 minutes. Requests refused during an episode count on the OTLP intake panel under reason="memory_pressure", as requests rather than spans, since they are turned away before the body is decoded. Reads 0 as well when the guard is off ([daemon] memory_high_water_pct = 0, the default) or on a host without a cgroup v2 memory limit, so OK does not say the guard is armed: /api/config does. The area behind the value is the state over the selected range.

panels.title: Events processed rate
panels.description: Spans accepted into the analysis pipeline per second, after non-I/O spans have been filtered out. Compare with the OTLP intake panel: a large gap between the two is normal, most spans in a trace are not I/O. A drop to zero while intake continues means the pipeline stopped consuming.

panels.title: Energy ingestion freshness
panels.description: Seconds since each CONFIGURED energy backend last returned a sample. A backend you did not configure draws nothing at all: its series is gated on perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured, because every energy gauge is pre-registered at zero and a successful scrape also sets the staleness gauge to zero, so without the gate 'not configured' and 'healthy' were the same flat line and an unconfigured install drew five of them per replica. Zero therefore means fresh. When an age climbs past its scrape interval the readings are stale and carbon attribution silently falls back to the built-in estimate, so the numbers stay plausible while no longer being measured.

defaults.noValue: No measured-energy backend configured. Carbon figures come from the built-in I/O proxy. See docs/ENERGY.md to plug in Alumet, Scaphandre, Kepler, Redfish or cloud SPECpower.

panels.title: Daemon memory (RSS)
panels.description: process_resident_memory_bytes per replica, from the standard process collector, which is registered on Linux only, so an empty panel on a macOS or Windows host is expected. Context for the memory-pressure stat: the guard compares the cgroup working set to [daemon] memory_high_water_pct, not this figure, and the two differ by the page cache, but a climb that never plateaus is the shape the guard exists to stop, and the level it plateaus at against resources.limits.memory is the number to size the limit from.

defaults.noValue: No process metrics: the process collector is registered on Linux only.

panels.title: Energy scrape outcome
panels.description: Scrape attempts per second on each CONFIGURED measured-energy backend, by outcome, gated on perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured like the freshness panel beside it. The freshness gauge alone cannot tell two states apart: a backend not scraped yet reads 0 during its first interval, and a backend failing every other tick keeps its age under the alert threshold. Here the first shows no success yet, the second a failed series beside the success one. Failure reasons are on perf_sentinel_<backend>_scrape_failed_total{reason}. What neither panel catches: an endpoint answering HTTP 200 with no sample matching the configured metric counts as a success and resets the age to 0, while carbon attribution has silently fallen back to the built-in estimate. That case is on the daemon's warn log after three such ticks and on the report's energy model tag. cloud_energy has a freshness gauge but no outcome counters, so it appears on the freshness panel only.

targets.expr:
sum by (job, instance, namespace, status) (rate(perf_sentinel_alumet_scrape_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on(job, instance, namespace)
(perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", backend="alumet"} == 1)

sum by (job, instance, namespace, status) (rate(perf_sentinel_scaphandre_scrape_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on(job, instance, namespace)
(perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", backend="scaphandre"} == 1)

sum by (job, instance, namespace, status) (rate(perf_sentinel_kepler_scrape_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on(job, instance, namespace)
(perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", backend="kepler"} == 1)

sum by (job, instance, namespace, status) (rate(perf_sentinel_redfish_scrape_total{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))
  and on(job, instance, namespace)
(perf_sentinel_energy_backend_configured{job=~"$job", namespace=~"$namespace", backend="redfish"} == 1)

defaults.noValue: No measured-energy backend configured, or none scraped yet.

panels.title: Runtime headroom and shedding
panels.description: Each runtime limit as a percentage of its configured cap, on the left axis. The advisor starts hinting at 90% (red line). The right axis shows shed batches, the traces they held, and dropped archive windows per second: when the analysis queue is full the daemon discards a whole batch rather than blocking ingestion, so those traces are never analysed and their findings never exist, and when the archive channel is full whole disclosure windows are dropped even though their findings were served live. A batch holds anywhere from one trace to a thousand, so PerfSentinelAnalysisShedding fires on the traces, past one per second over ten minutes, and the batch series says how the loss is chunked. Any sustained shedding means raising analysis_queue_capacity or giving the daemon more CPU, any sustained archive drops mean the disclosure archive under-reports the period. Pair evictions are the correlator recycling tracked pairs at the `max_tracked_pairs` cap, at which point /api/correlations returns an arbitrary subset with nothing on the output saying so. No alert covers it, since eviction at the cap is the steady state rather than a fault, and the tuning advisor in /api/export/report names the knob.

panels.title: Cardinality caps (overflow)
panels.description: Attributions per second that a per-run cardinality cap turned away, one series per cap. Five of the six fold into service="_other" or grouping="_other": the analysis-side series (findings, avoidable and analysed I/O ops) at 128 services and 512 (service, grouping) pairs, and the slow-span histogram at 64 services and 256 pairs, so their totals and sum by (service) stay exact and only the attribution of newly seen services or groupings coarsens. The ingest I/O counter folds groupings past 4096 pairs the same way, but a service past its 1024 cap is left out of the per-service counter rather than folded, so per-service throughput and measured-energy attribution undercount it. A flat zero is the normal state and none of these is an alert. A series that starts climbing means the fleet has more services or groupings than the cap, and the Service and Grouping variables show the folded ones under _other. The caps are per process lifetime: once reached they stay reached until the daemon restarts, so a rate that began after a burst of one-off service names (a load test, a canary naming scheme) keeps folding every service that came after it.

panels.title: OTLP span intake (received vs filtered)
panels.description: Span intake at the OTLP boundary. `filtered` are spans carrying no analyzable I/O operation, split by reason: `not_io` (internal spans, cache hits, middleware, inbound SERVER handlers) is normal and usually the majority, `non_sql_datastore` and `merged_db_span` are deliberate, and `missing_db_statement` and `missing_http_url` are the instrumentation gaps, a driver configured to omit query text or a client span with a method but no URL, which turn every request into zero events while every shipped alert stays green: this is the panel that shows them. `rejected` is split the same way: `channel_full` is the one the daemon loses work to and the only one PerfSentinelIngestRejecting fires on, `memory_pressure` is the admission guard (requests, counted before the body is decoded), while `parse_error` and `unsupported_media_type` are malformed requests from a producer, fixed in that producer and read here rather than paged on.

panels.title: Hub export (pending and dropped)
panels.description: State of the bounded PerfSentinelHub export buffer, for installs with [daemon.hub_export] configured, both series flat at zero otherwise. Pending is distinct finding signatures waiting for the next push, one per signature however often it recurs, so it plateaus at the fleet's distinct-problem count and climbs past it only when pushes fail. Dropped, on the right axis, is what the buffer gave up: entries evicted at hub_export.max_pending, a finding too large for the payload, and every entry of a batch the Hub refused with an unretryable 4xx. Nothing on the daemon side replays them, so a nonzero rate means the Hub's view of this daemon is short. No shipped alert: add rate(perf_sentinel_hub_export_dropped_total[15m]) > 0 through prometheusRule.additionalRules if you run the Hub.

panels.title: Report exports rate
panels.description: rate(perf_sentinel_export_report_requests_total). Tracks how often /api/export/report is consumed (CI snapshots, dev triage, daemon-Report to local-batch path).

panels.title: Energy per scoring window (kWh)
panels.description: Electricity attributed to the analysed workload for the most recent scoring window. Depending on configuration this is measured (an agent reading real power) or modelled from operation counts, and the report's model tag says which. Per-service and per-region detail is deliberately kept off /metrics to bound label cardinality, it lives in the query monitor.

panels.title: Carbon per scoring window (gCO2e)
panels.description: Operational emissions for the same window, summed across regions: energy multiplied by the local grid intensity. It moves with the workload but also with the grid, so a drop is not necessarily an optimisation, it can just be a cleaner hour. Manufacturing emissions are excluded here, fixing code does not un-manufacture hardware.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: The Prometheus job scraping perf-sentinel, one per install when several daemons share a Prometheus. All reads the fleet, pick one to keep staging apart from production. No .* fallback here, unlike Namespace: a scrape always sets job, so All expands to the jobs that carry perf-sentinel metrics and never to every target Prometheus knows.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Daemon namespace
list.description: Namespace the daemon install runs in (attached by the scrape), not a namespace of the analysed services. For the analysed workloads' namespace use Grouping.

list.name: grouping
list.label: Grouping
list.description: Grouping of the analysed traffic: the first attribute present from [detection] grouping_attributes (k8s.namespace.name, then service.namespace, by default), so on Kubernetes the namespace the workloads run in. Filters the Analysis row and narrows the Service list. The value alone is the label: two attributes with the same value share one entry. grouping="_other" is the fold bucket for (service, grouping) pairs past the per-run pair caps (512 on findings and the analysis-side I/O counters, 256 on the slow-span histogram, 4096 on the ingest counter); a folded pair keeps its service. A span that carried none of the configured attributes has an empty value, which Prometheus stores as no label at all: those series are only visible with All selected.

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: Analysed service (OTLP service.name). Filters the Analysis row, the Daemon health row is daemon-wide. service="_other" is the fold bucket for services past the per-run cardinality caps (128 on findings, 64 on the slow-span histogram): a service admitted at ingest but past an analysis cap has its findings there, not under its own name. Narrowed by Grouping.
